title: e-Learning 하도급 업체의 콘텐츠 개발과정에 관여하는 품질 저하요인 규명 및 개선방안에 관한 근거이론적 연구

abstracts.value: 본 연구의 목적은 e-Learning 교육과정 개발 현장에서 당면하고 있는 교육 품질저하 현상을 e-Learning 개발과정에서 가장 직접적으로 연관되어 있는 e-Learning 하도급 업체가 콘텐츠를 개발하는 과정에서 직면하고 있는 문제점을 중심으로 살펴보고 이에 따라 원인 및 개선방안을 밝혀보고자 한다. 즉 e-Learning 하도급 업체가 직면하고 있는 문제점과, e-Learning 콘텐츠가 어떤 과정을 통하여 기획, 설계, 개발, 납품되는지 살펴보았으며, 더 나아가 e-Learning 하도급 업체의 콘텐츠 품질확보를 위한 제도적 대응방안은 무엇인지 살펴보았다. 본 연구는 e-Learning 11업체를 대상으로 연구 문제를 귀납적으로 풀어나가기 위해 근거이론적 접근을 사용하였다. 본 연구의 결과는 다음과 같다. e-Learning의 품질 저하 요인은 첫째 e-Learning의 비용효과성을 지나치게 강조한 데서 기인한다. 둘째, 대기업, 브로커 업체, 하도급 업체 간의 불공정한 거래에서 생겨난다. 셋째, e-Learning 하도급 업체의 자체적인 역량 부족에 있다. 마지막으로, 현 고용보험의 정책도 e-Learning 콘텐츠 품질을 저하시키는 것으로 밝혀졌다. 이를 위한 대응방안으로는 첫째, e-Learning을 바라보는 생각의 변화가 요구된다. 둘째, 대기업, 브로커 업체, 하도급 업체간의 윤리적인관계 개선이 필요하다. 셋째, 산학협력체제 구축 및 제도적 활성화 방안을 마련해야 한다. 넷째, 고용보험 환급기준은 앞으로 교육 효율성 보다는 교육 효과성에 초점을 맞추어 개선될 필요가 있다.

New trends in the 21st century, identifying production method as various kinds of specialized items in small lots, seek for high performance through the way of complementary cooperation between main and subcontractors. The benefits of this new trend can lead to high performance when main and subcontractors develope close relationships of mutual dependance. But, instead, contractors and subcontractors has never been on equal footing, due to misuse of power by large contractors. Critical issues have been raised over those unstable relationships and many studies have tried to find alternative solutions to make contractors be in tandem with subcontractors. However, in spite of these efforts in other fields, no studies over relationships between e-Learning contractors and subcontractors can be found. The purpose of this study is to identify causes of constraining the quality of e-Learning programs in e-Learning subcontractors.
This study has the following questions: First, what is the limitation to sustainable development of e-Learning programs when subcontractors perform the development of e-learning programs? Second, in what process do subcontractors draw up plans, design, develop, and finally deliver e-learning programs? Third, what kind of alternative systematic policies could actually support for improving its quality? This study examined the perspectives of three kinds of contractors. This study is done with 11 contractors, was started in June, and completed in November. The contractors are 3 large firms, 4 brokers, and 4 subcontractors. The methodology in this study is based on the grounded theory, which is the methodology of choice for the real issues, found in the field, and for theorizing data in inductive ways. The coding process is divided into 3 ways: open coding, axial coding, and selective coding.
The research findings in this study is the following; First, the biggest cause in constraining the quality of the e-Learning program is the over-emphasis on cost-effectiveness rather than on the educational benefits. Second, the unfair business relationship between main and subcontractors and brokerages reduces the quality of e-Learning programs. The number of brokerages are relatively small, compared to the that of subcontractors; brokerages have a direct bearing of orders from big firms and subcontractors rely heavily on them. Therefore, the monolopoly of brokerage firms make necessary high commission expenses unavoidable for subcontractors and exacerbates the cost-effectiveness issue. Third, individuals involved in developing e-learning programs in subcontractors are not specialized enough to produce high-quality items. Limited working funds make subcontractors unable to employ experts or to advance high standards in developing competent educational programs. Finally, the supporting program for labor education, done by employment insurance also restricts its qualitative improvement. When first employing this policy, many opportunities for learning was given to employees. However, present evaluating standards for returning funds are fuzzy and unclear. Not least, the present standards are for evaluating quantitative participation in educational programs rather than qualitative improvement.
